/-!
# Conjecture 10.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup is embeddable in a direct
product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite groups?

An $FC$-group is a group in which every conjugacy class is finite. Following the conventions of
the Kourovka Notebook and of the theory of $FC$-groups (M. J. Tomkinson, *FC-groups*, Pitman,
1984), the direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$ of a family of groups is the *restricted*
direct product: the subgroup of the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ consisting of the
elements with only finitely many non-trivial coordinates. This convention matters: for every
$FC$-group $G$ the quotient $G/Z(G)$ embeds in the Cartesian product
$\prod_{x \in G} G/C_G(x^G)$ of finite groups (Baer), so for unrestricted products the question
would have a trivial positive answer.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.17
- M. J. Tomkinson, *FC-groups*, Research Notes in Mathematics 96, Pitman, 1984
-/

blocks.name: IsFCGroup

blocks.docstring:
A group $H$ is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups if there are finite groups
$F_i$, $i \in I$, and an injective homomorphism from $H$ into the Cartesian product
$\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ whose image lies in the restricted direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$,
that is, every element of the image has only finitely many non-trivial coordinates.

justification.closest_existing_considered: RestrictedProduct (Πʳ i, [F i, ⊥]) from Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.RestrictedProduct — equivalent but more exotic and topology-oriented; DFinsupp (Π₀) has only additive group structure; Function.mulSupport does not apply to dependent functions.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.17».IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups
justification.why_needed: No Mathlib notion of a group embedding into a (restricted) direct product of finite groups, nor of residual finiteness. Defined as an injective MonoidHom into ∀ i, F i (all F i finite groups) with every image element of finite support.

blocks.name: IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups
blocks.text:
/-- A group $H$ is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups if there are finite groups
$F_i$, $i \in I$, and an injective homomorphism from $H$ into the Cartesian product
$\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ whose image lies in the restricted direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$,
that is, every element of the image has only finitely many non-trivial coordinates. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : H →* ∀ i, F i), Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ h : H, {i | f h i ≠ 1}.Finite

theorem IsFCGroup.of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsFCGroup G := by

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over all FC-groups G (groups in which every conjugacy class is finite); 'embeddable in a direct product of finite groups' means embeddable in an unrestricted (Cartesian) product of finite groups, which is equivalent to being residually finite, so the Prop is: for every FC-group G, if the commutator subgroup G' is residually finite then so is G/Z(G) (Z(G) the center); the answer is asserted via answer(sorry) ↔ … as in the other Kourovka files.
claims.reviewer_why: c05 states the restricted-direct-product reading with the most literal bespoke definitions: IsFCGroup G := ∀ g, (conjugatesOf g).Finite; IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups H := ∃ finite groups F i and an injective hom H →* ∀ i, F i with every image element finitely supported. Derived subgroup is Mathlib's `commutator G` (= ⁅⊤,⊤⁆), G/Z(G) is `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G`, and the yes/no question is `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], ...` as in sibling Kourovka files. Three proven `category test` lemmas exercise the bespoke definitions. c02/c04/c08 are equivalent in content (c02 via Mathlib's RestrictedProduct, c08 fixes the index universe to Type); I used c05 for its transparency and docs, with light edits to the module docstring (references, attribution of Baer's theorem).

decomposition_objections.text: The slot notes assert that "embeddable in a direct product of finite groups" means embeddable in an unrestricted (Cartesian) product of finite groups, i.e. residually finite. This reading is wrong for this problem. For every FC-group G, Z(G) = ⋂_x C_G(x^G) is an intersection of finite-index normal subgroups (each conjugacy class x^G is finite, so its centralizer has finite index), hence G/Z(G) embeds in the Cartesian product ∏_x G/C_G(x^G) of finite groups. So under the Cartesian reading the answer is trivially "yes" for every FC-group, the hypothesis on G' is irrelevant, and the problem would not be open. In the FC-group literature (Tomkinson, "FC-groups", 1984; Robinson's convention Dr vs Cr) "direct product" means the restricted direct product (elements with finitely many non-trivial coordinates), and this is the reading under which the question (the converse of Tomkinson's theorem that G/Z(G) ∈ Dr-embeddable ⇒ G' Dr-embeddable) is non-trivial and open. I formalized the restricted-direct-product reading and did not follow the notes' residual-finiteness reading, since a faithful statement of the open problem cannot be trivially true.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup is embeddable in a direct
product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite groups?

An $FC$-group is a group in which every conjugacy class is finite. Following the conventions of
the Kourovka Notebook and of the theory of $FC$-groups (M. J. Tomkinson, *FC-groups*, Pitman,
1984), the direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$ of a family of groups is the *restricted*
direct product: the subgroup of the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ consisting of the
elements with only finitely many non-trivial coordinates. This convention matters: for every
$FC$-group $G$ the quotient $G/Z(G)$ embeds in the Cartesian product
$\prod_{x \in G} G/C_G(x^G)$ of finite groups (Baer), so for unrestricted products the question
would have a trivial positive answer.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.17
- M. J. Tomkinson, *FC-groups*, Research Notes in Mathematics 96, Pitman, 1984
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«10.17»

/-- A group $G$ is an $FC$-group if every conjugacy class of $G$ is finite. -/
def IsFCGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, (conjugatesOf g).Finite

/-- A group $H$ is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups if there are finite groups
$F_i$, $i \in I$, and an injective homomorphism from $H$ into the Cartesian product
$\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ whose image lies in the restricted direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$,
that is, every element of the image has only finitely many non-trivial coordinates. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : H →* ∀ i, F i), Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ h : H, {i | f h i ≠ 1}.Finite

/-- Every finite group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsFCGroup G :=
  fun _ => Set.toFinite _

/-- Every abelian group is an $FC$-group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsFCGroup.of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsFCGroup G := by
  intro g
  have : conjugatesOf g = {g} := by
    ext x
    simp [conjugatesOf, isConj_iff_eq, eq_comm]
  rw [this]
  exact Set.finite_singleton g

/-- Every finite group is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups.of_finite (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups G :=
  ⟨PUnit, fun _ => G, inferInstance, inferInstance, Pi.monoidHom fun _ => MonoidHom.id G,
    fun _ _ h => congrFun h PUnit.unit, fun _ => Set.toFinite _⟩

/--
(M. J. Tomkinson). Let $G$ be an $FC$-group whose derived subgroup $G'$ is embeddable in a direct
product of finite groups. Must $G/Z(G)$ be embeddable in a direct product of finite groups?

Here "direct product" is the restricted direct product $\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$, as is standard
in the theory of $FC$-groups; see `IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.17» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsFCGroup G →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (commutator G) →
      IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (G ⧸ Subgroup.center G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.17»

items: "Direct product of finite groups" is modelled as the restricted direct product: an injective hom f : H →* ∀ i, F i into a product of finite groups such that every f h has finite support {i | f h i ≠ 1}. This deviates from the decomposition notes (Cartesian product / residually finite), which would trivialize the problem; see decomposition_objections.
FC-group is modelled as ∀ g, (conjugatesOf g).Finite, i.e. every conjugacy class is finite (Mathlib's conjugatesOf g = {b | IsConj g b}).
Derived subgroup is Mathlib's `commutator G` (= ⁅⊤, ⊤⁆) and Z(G) is `Subgroup.center G`; G/Z(G) is `G ⧸ Subgroup.center G`.

G is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), as in the sibling Kourovka files; the index type and factors of the direct product live in the same universe as H. This loses nothing: the union of the supports of the image elements has cardinality ≤ max(|H|, ℵ₀), so any embedding can be re-indexed within the same universe.
Finite groups F i are given by `Finite (F i)`; the index type is arbitrary (possibly empty, in which case only the trivial group embeds).

The module docstring and theorem docstring state the restricted-product convention explicitly and briefly explain why it is essential (Cartesian reading is trivial). Three `category test` API theorems with complete proofs are included for the bespoke definitions (finite groups are FC, abelian groups are FC, finite groups embed in a direct product of finite groups).

reviewer_notes: Key adjudication: the decomposition note's gloss ('direct product' = unrestricted Cartesian product, i.e. residual finiteness) is rejected. Under that reading the problem is a classical theorem (Baer): for any FC-group G, each C_G(x^G) is a finite-index normal subgroup and their intersection is Z(G), so G/Z(G) is residually finite with no hypothesis on G' at all. Candidates c01, c03, c06, c07 formalize exactly this trivially-true statement (their `answer(sorry)` is provably True by elementary group theory), which cannot be a faithful rendering of an open Kourovka problem; they were rejected. The Kourovka Notebook (Kargapolov–Merzlyakov conventions) and Tomkinson's monograph *FC-groups* use 'direct product' (Dr) for the restricted product and 'Cartesian product' (Cr) for the unrestricted one; the question is Tomkinson's converse and is nontrivial only for uncountable G (P. Hall: countable periodic residually finite FC-groups embed in Dr of finite groups). The four restricted-reading candidates (c02, c04, c05, c08) agree on content; all compile. Universe choice (index type and factors in the same universe as H) is WLOG since finite groups are small and only the union of finitely many supports per element matters. Residual uncertainty (~0.14) reflects the interpretive call on 'direct product' against the table's note, though I consider the trivialization argument decisive.
